posts.message: Fresh run of stone-ground yellow grits off the mill this week. 2 lb bags at the shop Friday and Saturday.
Up Mount Mitchell with the grandkids today. 52 degrees at the top on Labor Day weekend.
First real heat of the summer out at Bent Creek today. Found a shady creek crossing and sat there longer than I meant to.
Poplars just starting to turn along the Bent Creek trails. Nearly had the loop to myself this afternoon.
Open today 7 to 3. Pumpkin loaf and cider donuts on the counter, and the last honey oat loaves of the week.
Admin day. The market tent is out of the garage, new weights are in the van, and the first Saturday is this week.
Haywood Road streetscape plan is on the City Council agenda tomorrow night. If you care about the bike lanes or the parking, now's the time to email them.
Market season starts tomorrow. We're at the North Asheville Farmers Market every Saturday, 8 to noon, through the Saturday before Thanksgiving. Rye, country loaves and rhubarb galettes.
Hiring a morning baker, four days a week starting in October. Lamination experience is a plus. Early mornings are not optional. Message me.
Update for anyone else running a Bongard: Smoky Mtn Refrigeration fabricated a steam tube for me in four days. Saved my spring. Worth a call.
I'm teaching a sourdough class at Sourwood Culinary Studio next Monday, May 11. It filled up fast. They keep a waitlist if you want in on the next one.

Reminder from the board: certificates of insurance are due Friday 5/15. $1M general liability, with the market listed as certificate holder and additional insured. No certificate on file, no setup starting 5/16.
Mother's Day weekend: extra cinnamon rolls and lemon loaves at the market on Saturday, and strawberry shortcakes in the café case on Sunday.
Hazel's home for the summer. First thing she did was eat a cinnamon roll standing over the sink. Nothing has changed.
happy mother's day to the hardest working woman i know, who is at work right now lol 💐
Ran the Sunday close solo so the boss could make her flight to the expo in Chicago. Drawer balanced, walk-in logged, nobody cried 👍
Chicago for the baking expo. Two days of watching people shape bread faster than should be legal. Back in Asheville Tuesday.
Twelve years in restaurants and tonight was my last shift as a GM. I start with a catering company Monday. Weekends off. I don't know what people do with weekends.
If you've bought bread at our market table this year, you've met Sasha. She keeps the line moving, remembers your usual, and has never once run out of change.
Vendor parking moves to the upper lot starting Saturday 6/13 while the lower lot gets restriped. And please keep weights on all four tent legs. These afternoon storms are no joke.
Does anyone know a tomato that will put up with a mostly shady yard? Asking as a famously terrible gardener.
Craggy Gardens this afternoon. Rhododendrons right at peak. Gloria and Ben set a pace I'm still recovering from.
Our walk-in started reading 46 Sunday afternoon. Smoky Mtn is coming out Tuesday at noon. Does anyone have a backup refrigeration tech they trust, for next time?
Four extra country loaves from the market on my porch on Westwood. Free, first come.
Tried laminating croissant dough at home without a sheeter. My arms would like a word 😅
We're open on the Fourth. Market 8 to noon and the café 7 to 3, like any Saturday. Blueberry hand pies at both.
Selling our old tabletop sheeter, the listing is up on Marketplace. Runs fine, we just outgrew it. Happy to show it running to anyone serious.
If your latte has a fern on it, Noor probably made it. Say hi next time you're in.
Power's out on our end of Westwood. Duke says a tree came down on a line and they're estimating 11:30 tonight. Anybody have ice to spare?
tournament weekend in Hendersonville. 2 wins, a tie and one very sunburned goalie. proud of these kids
Block party is Saturday 8/22 at 4! Walt is firing up the smoker again. The sign-up sheet for sides and drinks is on my porch, grab a pen.
canned 32 jars of tomato sauce since sunday. borrowed pot, neighbor's tomatoes, my own burns 🍅🔥
Last peach hand pies of the summer this Saturday, plus tomato focaccia, at the market while they last.
Hazel's back for year two. Car packed to the roof, plus a cooler of bread she swears she'll freeze.
Meet Marco. He's in at 4 with me every café morning, shapes a good share of the bread you buy, and takes in every delivery while I'm on the bench. Say hi if you see him at dawn.
Block party on our street this afternoon. Walt smoked a brisket for fourteen hours and it was gone in twenty minutes. Good neighbors.
Fourteen hours on the smoker for the block party and I came home with an empty pan. Best street in Asheville.

Fall schedule is set. Last market is Saturday 11/21. Halloween falls on a Saturday, so costumes are welcome and the board will have candy at the info tent. Load-out has to be done by 12:45 so the lot can reopen.
Open all Labor Day weekend except Monday. Find us at the market Saturday morning and at the café Saturday and Sunday until 3.
First apples this Saturday! Ginger Golds and Galas. Honeycrisp is about two weeks out.
Fall wildflower honey is jarred. Darker than last year, with lots of goldenrod in it. The dry August means there's less of it, so don't wait. Saturdays at the North Asheville market.
The rye and whole grain class at Sourwood Culinary Studio on the 21st is full. They added a bench to fit two more. Thank you, all of you.
New fall menu at Sorrel & Pine starts Friday. Trout from up the road, the first apples, and a pork shoulder that takes two days.
Lake Powhatan loop and then the long way back. About six miles, and the first Sunday that felt like fall.
Fall menu starts Wednesday. Pumpkin loaf every day we're open, apple cider donuts Saturdays and Sundays only, and June has a few more things coming.
Honey oat loaves are back for the fall. The honey is Hollow Oak's new wildflower harvest, darker this year and full of goldenrod, and it makes a great loaf.
Heads up from the city: Haywood Road repaving starts in November. We'll stay open through it and post parking tips once we know which blocks go first.
City notice on every door today: Westwood repaving starts Thursday 10/1. No street parking 7am to 5pm while they work.
Seven Saturdays to go! The board is gauging interest in a small winter market on the first Saturday of December, January and February. Reply to the board email by 10/30 if you're in.
Seven market Saturdays left this season. The last one is November 21. Rye and cider donuts every week until then.
Whipped feta, since three people asked: feta, a spoonful of Greek yogurt, lemon zest, blitz until smooth. Warm some honey with chili flakes and pour it over. Bread required.
Looking ahead to 2027: prepared food vendors need a current county food permit uploaded to the vendor portal by Friday 12/4. Lots of permits expire 11/30, so renew early.
Craggy is peaking up high. Go this week if you can. The visitor center lot was full by ten on Sunday.

Thanksgiving pie preorders are open. Apple, pecan, pumpkin, and bourbon sweet potato. Pickup is Wednesday 11/25 at the café, 7 to 3. Send us a message here to order. Orders close when the oven schedule is full.
Pie season check-in: who's doing Thanksgiving preorders this year, and when's your cutoff? We're closing ours 11/20.
Chocolate rye cookies have been the staff meal favorite all summer. June finally talked me into putting them on the menu. As of this morning they're in the case.
Halloween is a market Saturday this year. Come in costume on the 31st. The market board is handing out candy at the info tent, and we'll have pumpkin loaf and cider donuts at our table.
Frost advisory up high tonight. If you're heading to Craggy this weekend, bring real layers.
Market season is almost over and I'm already sad about it 🥲 Five more Saturdays!

marketplace_listings.title: 10x10 pop-up canopy, white
marketplace_listings.description: Our old market canopy, retired a couple of seasons ago and taking up room in the garage. Frame is solid and all four legs lock, one small tear on the valance, and the carry bag zipper is shot. Weights not included. Pickup in West Asheville, evenings.

marketplace_listings.title: Tabletop dough sheeter, 20 inch
marketplace_listings.description: Reversible tabletop sheeter with 20 inch rollers, single phase. Belts replaced last year and the scrapers are clean. We moved up to a floor model. Pickup only in Asheville, bring a second person, it's heavy.

marketplace_listings.title: Half sheet pans, lot of 10
marketplace_listings.description: 18x26 aluminum, commercial weight. A few rock a little on a flat counter but they're fine for cookies or roasting vegetables. We replaced our set. $25 takes all ten, not splitting. Pickup in West Asheville.

marketplace_listings.title: Bannetons, 9 inch round, set of 12
marketplace_listings.description: Rattan proofing baskets with linen liners. Used but clean and fully dried out. We switched to ovals. $60 for all 12.
